title: Nab-paclitaxel · Days 1, 8 and 15 of 28

agents.name: Nab-paclitaxel
agents.mechanism: Disrupts cell division by stabilising microtubules
agents.explanation: This formulation carries paclitaxel with albumin, a protein. It interferes with the structures cells use to divide. Its dosing and allergy precautions differ from ordinary paclitaxel.
agents.watch: Report numbness, tingling, weakness or problems with daily tasks before the next dose. Tell staff about an infusion reaction; new cough or breathlessness needs prompt assessment.
risks: Numbness / tingling or weakness, sometimes lasting
Low blood counts, infection and sepsis
Hair loss, fatigue and muscle / joint aches
Infusion reactions; uncommon serious lung inflammation

phases_title: Treatment, reassessment and the next decision
phases_note: This card describes one active chemotherapy schedule. There is no automatic maintenance phase; continuing, changing or stopping treatment follows clinical review.
timeline_note: Treatment markers show the planned days. Symptom bands show broad possibilities, not measured risk curves or guaranteed symptom-free days.
safety_note: Fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell needs prompt advice on any day, including planned treatment-free weeks.
teachback: Which days are treatment days, what checks are due before the next dose, and who is arranging and reviewing the next scan?
consent_support: Discuss the exact indication, expected benefit, alternatives, uncertainty, serious and lasting risks, contraception and fertility, venous access, monitoring and the urgent contact plan. Explain off-label schedule and record the local approval / consent process.
urgent_extra: Report new cough or breathlessness, fever or sudden illness promptly. Tell staff immediately about an infusion reaction or pain at the infusion site. Report numbness, tingling or loss of daily function before the next dose.

support.title: Supportive medicines
support.text: Routine allergy premedicines are usually not required for nab-paclitaxel. Prior reactions require individual review; treatment is still given where a serious reaction can be managed.

support.title: Everyday care
support.text: Keep gently active as tolerated, pace rest and activity, and report nerve symptoms before the next dose.

support.title: Tests and appointments
support.text: Ask who books each test, when it is due and who reviews the result. Tell the team if an expected appointment has not arrived.

support.title: Correct medicine and schedule
support.text: This is a 100 mg/m² weekly schedule with a planned break. It is not a divided version of the 260 mg/m² three-weekly dose. Its dose-reduction levels are different.

questions.q: Which treatment days and breaks should I expect?
questions.a: Nab-paclitaxel on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle, with a planned week off on Day 22. Continue while beneficial and tolerated. This off-label schedule requires specific consent.

questions.q: When do I need blood tests, an ECG or echo?
questions.a: FBC, renal and liver profile at baseline and before each cycle; the NCCP source additionally specifies FBC on Day 8. The team decides if extra blood tests are needed, including before Day 15. Cardiac assessment when clinically indicated by symptoms, significant cardiac history or prior anthracycline therapy. ECG does not replace an echo. Baseline echo / MUGA if significant cardiac history or prior anthracycline exposure; repeat cardiac tests if clinically indicated. No fixed routine 3-month echo schedule is specified for this medicine alone.

questions.q: When will we know whether treatment is helping?
questions.a: For metastatic breast cancer, ESMO recommends response evaluation generally every 2–4 months, adjusted to disease, treatment and symptoms. Agree the scan type, due window and result-review appointment; symptoms can prompt earlier assessment.

questions.q: Where do surgery or radiotherapy fit?
questions.a: These are advanced-disease regimens. Surgery or radiotherapy is used only for a defined local or symptom-control purpose. The oncology and radiation teams decide whether chemotherapy continues, pauses or precedes radiation; no routine overlap is implied.
Tumour markers, when useful for the cancer being treated, supplement clinical assessment and imaging. A marker result alone should not determine treatment failure or a treatment change.

questions.q: Does a port mean a pump at home?
questions.a: No. A port is a route into a vein. Staff disconnect the infusion and remove the port needle after the visit when appropriate; removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure.

evidence.title: Weekly nab-paclitaxel: phase II schedule-specific evidence
evidence.intro: Evidence belongs to the cancer, population and schedule actually studied.
evidence.population: Patients with metastatic breast cancer progressing after conventional taxanes; 106 received 100 mg/m² and 75 received 125 mg/m² on Days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days.
evidence.interpretation: Supports activity and tolerability of the weekly 100 mg/m² schedule. Separate randomized phase II first-line evidence included 100 and 150 mg/m² weekly schedules (Gradishar 2009). Neither trial specifically proves outcomes in a population selected for standard-paclitaxel hypersensitivity. The significant PFS comparison reported for 150 mg/m² in Gradishar 2009 must not be assigned to NCCP 100 mg/m². The weekly schedule is outside the licensed Irish indication described in NCCP 00736 and needs the specified consent/local approval pathway. Do not copy the q21-day phase III efficacy numbers.

items.title: Indication
items.text: Metastatic breast cancer after anthracycline failure or when anthracyclines are unsuitable; this regimen is intended when hypersensitivity or intolerance prevents standard paclitaxel. It is an off-label schedule.

items.title: Dose and formulation
items.text: 100 mg/m². This is a 100 mg/m² weekly schedule with a planned break. It is not a divided version of the 260 mg/m² three-weekly dose. Its dose-reduction levels are different.

The weekly schedule is outside the licensed Irish indication described in NCCP 00736 and needs the specified consent/local approval pathway. Do not copy the q21-day phase III efficacy numbers.

items.text: DEXA is not a routine test for this chemotherapy alone. Assess fracture risk and bone density when indicated by endocrine treatment, ovarian suppression or other clinical risks; repeat according to the relevant plan.

chronology_notes.title: A delay changes the treatment plan
chronology_notes.text: Do not move, double or make up doses yourself. A delayed infusion does not automatically move an already-due scan or heart test.

chronology_notes.title: Review milestone
chronology_notes.text: Review neuropathy and function at each visit. Response imaging follows the agreed metastatic breast plan; symptoms can bring assessment forward.

steps.title: Before the first visit
steps.text: Confirm the indication, baseline bloods, required cardiac checks, medicines review and consent before the first infusion.

steps.title: Plan venous access
steps.text: A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. If a port is chosen, a trained team inserts it in a separate procedure with local anaesthetic and sometimes sedation; the team explains fasting, blood-thinner and wound instructions.

steps.title: Infusion day
steps.text: Each nab-paclitaxel dose is infused over 30 minutes. Your full visit also includes checks, preparation and any observation. Staff observe for reactions. Report burning, pain, swelling or leakage at the infusion site immediately.

steps.title: Home and next review
steps.text: This regimen does not routinely need a take-home infusion pump. Staff disconnect the infusion; a port is de-accessed when appropriate. Keep line-care and next-visit instructions.

details.title: Port insertion and removal
details.text: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: PICC care and urgent line symptoms
details.text: A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.

details.title: Visit length
details.text: Each nab-paclitaxel dose is infused over 30 minutes. Your full visit also includes checks, preparation and any observation. A port is optional access, not a requirement for a take-home pump. This regimen has no routine ambulatory pump.

details.title: Premedication
details.text: Routine allergy premedicines are usually not required for nab-paclitaxel. Prior reactions require individual review; treatment is still given where a serious reaction can be managed.
